title: The Three Billy Goats Gruff
author: Traditional Norwegian Tale
description: Three goats must outsmart a fierce troll to cross a bridge to greener pastures.
summary:
Once upon a time, three billy goats lived near a river. Their names were Little Billy Goat Gruff, Middle Billy Goat Gruff, and Big Billy Goat Gruff. On the other side of the river, there was a beautiful green hillside with sweet grass. The goats wanted to eat the grass and grow fat.

To reach the hillside, the goats had to cross a bridge over the river. But under the bridge lived a terrible troll. He had big eyes, a huge nose, and long sharp claws. He ate anyone who tried to cross his bridge.

First, Little Billy Goat Gruff stepped onto the bridge. Trip, trap! Trip, trap! The troll jumped up and roared, "Who is crossing my bridge? I will eat you for breakfast!" But Little Billy Goat Gruff said, "Please do not eat me. Wait for my brother. He is much bigger and tastier!" The troll agreed and let him pass.

Next, Middle Billy Goat Gruff crossed the bridge. Trip, trap! Trip, trap! The troll jumped up again. "Who dares cross my bridge?" he growled. "Wait for my big brother," said Middle Billy Goat Gruff. "He is the biggest and most delicious!" The troll agreed and let him pass too.

Finally, Big Billy Goat Gruff walked onto the bridge. TRIP, TRAP! TRIP, TRAP! The whole bridge shook. The troll roared, "Now I will eat you!" But Big Billy Goat Gruff lowered his great horns and charged. He tossed the troll high into the air, and the troll fell into the river and was never seen again. The three billy goats lived happily on the green hillside and grew very fat indeed.

title: Goldilocks and the Three Bears
author: Traditional English Tale
description: A curious girl enters the bears' cottage and tries their porridge, chairs, and beds.
summary:
Once upon a time, three bears lived together in a little house in the forest. There was a great big Papa Bear, a middle-sized Mama Bear, and a tiny Baby Bear. One morning they made porridge for breakfast. The porridge was too hot to eat, so they went for a walk in the forest while it cooled down.

While the bears were away, a little girl named Goldilocks came to their house. She had golden curly hair and was very curious. She knocked on the door, but no one answered. She opened the door and walked right in.

Goldilocks saw three bowls of porridge on the table. She tasted Papa Bear's porridge. "Too hot!" she said. She tasted Mama Bear's porridge. "Too cold!" she said. She tasted Baby Bear's porridge. "Just right!" she said, and ate it all up.

Then Goldilocks saw three chairs. She sat in Papa Bear's chair. "Too hard!" she said. She sat in Mama Bear's chair. "Too soft!" she said. She sat in Baby Bear's tiny chair. "Just right!" she said. But it was too small, and it broke into pieces.

Feeling tired, Goldilocks went upstairs and found three beds. Papa Bear's bed was too hard. Mama Bear's bed was too soft. Baby Bear's little bed was just right! She fell fast asleep.

Soon the three bears came home. "Someone has been eating my porridge!" roared Papa Bear. "Someone has been sitting in my chair and broken it!" cried Baby Bear. Then they went upstairs and found Goldilocks asleep in Baby Bear's bed. She woke up, saw the three bears, screamed, jumped out of the window, and ran home as fast as she could. The three bears never saw her again.

title: Little Red Riding Hood
author: Brothers Grimm
description: A little girl in a red cloak must be brave when she meets a tricky wolf in the forest.
summary:
Once upon a time, there was a sweet little girl who lived in a village near the forest. Her grandmother had made her a beautiful red velvet cloak with a hood, and she wore it everywhere. Everyone called her Little Red Riding Hood.

One day, her mother said, "Your grandmother is sick and resting in bed. Please take her this basket of bread and butter and jam." Little Red Riding Hood was happy to help. "Do not leave the path, and do not talk to strangers," said her mother. Little Red Riding Hood promised and skipped off into the forest.

Deep in the forest, she met a big grey wolf. The wolf wanted to eat her, but he heard a woodcutter nearby, so he was clever instead. "Where are you going, little girl?" he asked in a gentle voice. "To my grandmother's house," she answered. "She lives in the cottage past the oak trees." Then she said goodbye and continued on her way.

The wolf ran ahead by a different path and arrived at Grandmother's house first. He knocked on the door and said in a soft voice, "It is your granddaughter, Grandmother!" The old woman called out, "Come in, dear." The wolf came inside and swallowed Grandmother whole. Then he put on her nightgown and cap and got into her bed.

When Little Red Riding Hood arrived, she noticed something strange. "What big eyes you have, Grandmother!" she said. "All the better to see you with!" said the wolf. "What big ears you have!" "All the better to hear you with!" "What big teeth you have!" "All the better to EAT you with!" cried the wolf. But the woodcutter heard her scream, rushed inside, and rescued Little Red Riding Hood and her grandmother. They all lived safely ever after.

title: Hansel and Gretel
author: Brothers Grimm
description: Two children lost in the forest find a gingerbread house — but the old woman inside has a dark secret.
summary:
Once upon a time, a woodcutter and his wife lived at the edge of a great forest with their two children, Hansel and Gretel. The family was very poor. One night, as the children lay in bed, they heard their stepmother tell their father to take the children deep into the forest and leave them there so that the family might survive.

Hansel had heard the plan. Early the next morning, he filled his pockets with small white pebbles that shone like silver in the moonlight. As their father led them into the forest, Hansel secretly dropped the pebbles one by one along the path. When their father left them alone, Gretel began to cry. But Hansel said, "Do not worry. I know the way home." When the moon rose, the white pebbles lit up the path, and the children followed them safely back home.

But their stepmother sent them into the forest a second time. This time, Hansel had no pebbles. Instead he dropped a trail of breadcrumbs. But when they tried to follow the crumbs home, they were all gone — the birds had eaten every one. The children were truly lost.

Wandering through the dark forest, they came upon a wonderful little house made entirely of gingerbread, cake, and candy. They began to eat hungrily. But the house belonged to a wicked old witch who lured children inside, then locked them up and ate them. She grabbed Hansel and locked him in a cage to fatten him up. She forced Gretel to cook and clean.

Every day the witch checked if Hansel was fat enough by asking him to stick out his finger. Clever Hansel always stuck out a thin chicken bone instead. One day the witch grew impatient and decided to cook Hansel right away. She told Gretel to climb into the oven to check if it was hot. Gretel guessed her plan. "I do not know how," she said sweetly. "Show me." The witch leaned inside to demonstrate, and Gretel pushed her in and slammed the door. She freed Hansel, and together they filled their pockets with the witch's jewels and found their way home, where their kind father welcomed them with great joy.

title: Jack and the Beanstalk
author: Traditional English Tale
description: A boy trades the family cow for magic beans and discovers a giant's castle in the clouds.
summary:
Once upon a time, a poor boy named Jack lived with his mother. They had nothing left to eat and only one old cow. "Take the cow to market and sell her," said his mother. On the way, Jack met a strange old man. "I will give you these magic beans for your cow," said the man. Jack thought that sounded wonderful and made the trade.

When Jack arrived home without any money, his mother was furious. She threw the beans out of the window and sent Jack to bed without supper. But the next morning, Jack looked out and saw an enormous beanstalk reaching up through the clouds. He began to climb.

At the top of the beanstalk, Jack found himself in a magical land. In the distance, he could see a huge stone castle. A giant woman stood at the door. "Please may I have some breakfast?" Jack asked. She was kind and gave him bread and milk. But then the floor shook. BOOM! BOOM! BOOM! "That is my husband coming home," she whispered. "He eats boys for breakfast. Hide quickly!"

Jack hid inside a large pot. The giant came in roaring, "Fee, fi, fo, fum! I smell the blood of an Englishman!" His wife said it was only the smell of dinner. The giant sat down, ate a huge meal, and then commanded, "Bring me my golden harp!" The harp played beautiful music and the giant fell fast asleep.

Jack crept out, grabbed the golden harp, and ran. But the harp cried out, "Master! Master!" The giant woke up and chased Jack to the beanstalk. Jack climbed down as fast as he could. "Mother! Bring me the axe!" he shouted. She handed it up and Jack chopped the beanstalk with all his might. CRASH! The giant fell to the ground and was never seen again. Jack and his mother sold the golden harp and lived happily ever after.

title: The Tortoise and the Hare
author: Aesop
description: A slow tortoise challenges a boastful hare to a race — with a surprising result.
summary:
Once upon a time, a hare was always boasting about how fast he could run. "No one in the forest is faster than me!" he would say. A tortoise who lived nearby grew tired of hearing this. "Then let us have a race," said the tortoise calmly. All the animals in the forest laughed. How could a slow tortoise race a fast hare?

On the day of the race, all the animals gathered at the starting line. The fox waved his tail, and they were off! The hare shot forward like an arrow and was soon far ahead. He looked back and could not even see the tortoise. "I have so much time," he thought. "I will take a little nap under this oak tree."

Meanwhile, the tortoise kept walking. Step by step, slowly and steadily, he moved along the path. He did not stop. He did not look behind him. He just kept going.

When the hare woke up, he stretched and yawned. Then he looked down the road and his eyes went wide. Far in the distance, the tortoise was almost at the finish line! The hare ran as fast as he could, but it was too late. The tortoise crossed the finish line first. All the animals cheered.

"How did you beat me?" panted the hare. The tortoise smiled. "Slow and steady wins the race," he said quietly.

title: The Town Mouse and the Country Mouse
author: Aesop
description: Two mice discover that a life of luxury is not worth the constant danger it brings.
summary:
Once there was a Country Mouse who lived in a cosy little hole at the roots of an oak tree. He ate nuts and berries and slept on soft moss. It was a simple life, but it was peaceful and safe.

One day his cousin, the Town Mouse, came to visit. The Country Mouse offered his best food: some dried corn, some wheat, and a little piece of cheese. But the Town Mouse turned up his nose. "Is this really all you eat?" he said. "Come and visit me in the city. I will show you how to live properly!"

The Country Mouse was curious, so he agreed. That night they arrived at a grand house in the city. The Town Mouse led him to a magnificent dining table covered with the remains of a great feast. There was bread and honey, cake and fruit, and all kinds of delicious things. The Country Mouse could not believe his eyes. He began to eat happily.

But suddenly, two enormous cats burst through the door, meowing and hissing. The mice ran and hid in a tiny crack in the wall, trembling with fear. When the danger had passed, the Town Mouse said, "Come! Let us go back and eat!" But the Country Mouse shook his head.

"No thank you," he said. "You may have all the fine food in the world, but I would rather eat my simple corn in peace than feast on cake while living in fear." And he went back to his cosy home in the country, where he lived happily and quietly for the rest of his days.

title: The Goose That Laid the Golden Eggs
author: Aesop
description: A farmer discovers his goose lays golden eggs — but his greed destroys everything.
summary:
Once upon a time, a farmer and his wife lived on a small farm. They kept a flock of geese, and every morning the farmer collected the eggs and took them to the market to sell. It was a simple life, but they were happy.

One morning, the farmer went out to collect the eggs as usual. When he reached into the first nest, he pulled out an egg that was heavy and bright and shone like the sun. It was solid gold! He could not believe his eyes. He ran to show his wife, and she was just as amazed.

The next morning, there was another golden egg. And the morning after that, another. Every single day, the magical goose laid one perfect golden egg. Slowly, the farmer and his wife became rich. They built a bigger house and bought fine clothes and ate the best food in the village.

But as time went by, the farmer grew impatient. "Why should we wait for one egg a day?" he said to his wife. "If we cut the goose open, we can have all the golden eggs at once and be rich immediately!" His wife agreed. So the farmer took his knife and cut open the goose. But inside, there were no golden eggs at all. It was just an ordinary goose.

Now the farmer and his wife had no golden eggs and no goose. Their greed had destroyed the very thing that made them wealthy.
